audit.whatIsWrong: The full-layer level chart said 'Skill' for Levels 1 through 6 while the content layer and the packet levelChart both said 'Viktor' for those same five rows. The page rendered two different answers to 'who wins Level 1'.
audit.why: Emerald+ win rate is 45.46% over 1465 games, and both the packet chart and content win[0..4] read Viktor. Mechanically Viktor holds the early lane: Siphon Power (Q) is a 9s shield plus an auto reset, Gravity Field (W) is a 17s 800-range zone that stuns anyone who stays, and Hextech Ray (E) clears the wave from 12s at rank 1. Azir pre-Nashor's has soldier autos and a 22s escape.
audit.corrected: phases[0..4].side moved to Viktor with every why rewritten in the same proposal to explain Viktor winning that stage. content win[0..4] already read Viktor and were left alone; ratings left alone because their polarity is ambiguous.

audit.whatIsWrong: Spike text named the wrong abilities ('Death Ray', 'Chaos Storm', 'Hex Core upgrades') and the level 6 spike did not carry a cooldown.
audit.why: The kit file is authority: Viktor's E is Hextech Ray, his R is Arcane Storm, and his passive is Glorious Evolution granting Hex Fragments that augment an ability every 100. Arcane Storm is 120/100/80s; Emperor's Divide is 120/105/90s.
audit.corrected: Names corrected across spikes[0..3], early/mid/late, whys and wants. Real cooldowns added: Arcane Storm 120s at rank 1 and 80s at rank 3, Emperor's Divide 120s at rank 1.

audit.whatIsWrong: The decisive interactions were never stated. Nothing on the page mentioned that Siphon Power is an auto-attack reset, that Gravity Field only stuns if you remain inside it, or that Shifting Sands is the exit from that circle.
audit.why: Viktor's Q text reads 'empowers his next basic attack' and carries the autoReset flag — his burst opens with an auto, so the wind-up is the tell, not the spell cast. Gravity Field 'slows enemies caught within its radius. Enemies who stay in the field for too long become stunned' — leaving early denies the stun entirely. Azir's E is a dash that leaves on 22s at rank 1, and Gravity Field does not ground, so the dash out is available.
audit.corrected: Auto-reset tell written into tradeBad and breakdown.trading; the leave-the-circle-before-the-stun rule written into breakdown.cooldowns, report[5].t and phases[2].why with the real 22s Shifting Sands cooldown.

audit.whatIsWrong: breakdown.cooldowns contained no digit at all — defect catalogue item 3.
audit.why: It is the field that holds real cooldowns and every number was available in the kits.
audit.corrected: Rewrote with Gravity Field 17/16/15/14/13s at 800 range, Hextech Ray 12s at rank 1 falling to 8s at rank 5, and Shifting Sands 22s at rank 1.

audit.whatIsWrong: The suspect name flagged in the packet ('Death Ray' at wants.you[1]) was real, and the same error appeared in five more places along with 'Chaos Storm' in four places and 'Hex Core' in three.
audit.why: Kit file gives Hextech Ray (E), Arcane Storm (R), and Glorious Evolution / Hex Fragments (P).

audit.whatIsWrong: Copy-paste bleed: dosFull[1].d was the tradeGood string verbatim, dontsFull[2].d was the tradeBad string verbatim, and dosFull[0].d and dosFull[2].d explained something unrelated to their titles.
audit.why: Defect catalogue item 2. The title promises one thing and the body explains another.
audit.corrected: All four bodies rewritten to match their own titles, grounded in Viktor's ranges and Azir's mana costs.

audit.whatIsWrong: breakdown.wave was Azir boilerplate that would read identically against any mid laner.
audit.why: Viktor's Hextech Ray is a line wave clear on 12/11/10/9/8s — Azir cannot win the shove war before Nashor's, which changes which wave state he should want.
audit.corrected: Rewritten around not out-pushing Hextech Ray and crashing before Gravity Field comes back.

audit.whatIsWrong: enemyWin, ahead, breakdown.carry, breakdown.early, breakdown.mid and breakdown.feeding were all name-swap templates.
audit.why: Template sweep. Each could be pasted onto a different enemy with only the champion name changed.
audit.corrected: Each regrounded: enemyWin on the stun-into-full-combo sequence, ahead and feeding on denying Hex Fragments, carry on Viktor needing 600 range to threaten, mid on the 100s rank-2 Arcane Storm window.

edits.before: Best wave: a controlled slow push you crash with soldier autos — the crash funds your roam, your plates, and your scuttle-fight presence. Crash timing: the crash is a timer you set — reset, plate, or roam, but never just because.
edits.after: Best wave: you cannot out-push Hextech Ray, so hold the wave near your side and let it come — a slow push crashed with soldier autos is the only shove he cannot answer for free. Worst wave: frozen at his tower with Shifting Sands down, because Gravity Field lands on a stationary target. Crash timing: crash before his W comes back, not after.

edits.before: Viktor simply outclasses you in the early lane — Gravity Field denies your soldier zone control, Death Ray out-ranges your poke, and his wave clear from Hex Core upgrades lets him push you under tower repeatedly. Play passively, prioritize CS over trades, and look to your jungler for help since standing and trading is a losing proposition until your kit catches up.

edits.before: Level 6 brings Chaos Storm online for him, which is still a strong zone-control ultimate, but this is also the point where your own kit starts to close the gap — soldier count and your ultimate give you comparable area denial for the first time. It's no longer a lost lane, just an even fight where positioning and cooldown tracking matter more than raw stats.
edits.after: Level 6 brings Arcane Storm online for him, a 120s ultimate that follows you through your own soldiers, but this is the point where your kit closes the gap — Emperor's Divide gives you comparable area denial for the first time. edits.before: By full items this becomes a genuine skill matchup — Viktor's Chaos Storm and your soldier walls both zone space effectively, and neither side has a clean statistical edge. notes: Chart fix: full phases[0..4].side moved Skill->Viktor as one atomic group with matching rating and why rewrites; content win[0..4] already read Viktor so no content chart edit was needed. Win rate 45.46% over 1465 games is below even, but diff/diffRating/carryRating/tone were left alone because Azir's global baseline is itself sub-50 and I could not tell from the data whether 45.46 warrants moving EVEN to HARD — see questionsForUser. Viktor R is Arcane Storm and E is Hextech Ray per the kit file; the page carried 'Chaos Storm' and 'Death Ray' throughout and both were corrected. Viktor's R carries a derived 'channel: interruptible' flag but Riot's description only says it can be redirected by Viktor — I did not write any claim that Emperor's Divide or any CC interrupts Arcane Storm. Also unverified and therefore unwritten: whether Azir's Emperor's Divide wall blocks Hextech Ray's projectile, and whether Gravity Field's stun is tenacity-reducible. Ratings left untouched: phases[N].rating appears to encode stage DIFFICULTY (higher = harder for Azir) rather than Azir-favourability, judging by the vladimir entry where the two Vladimir-winning rows carry 7/10 against an overall diffRating of 7/10 while the neutral rows carry 5/10. I did not want to guess the polarity across five rows, so side and why moved and rating did not.
